title: Number of Ways to Build House of Cards
summary: Given an integer n representing the number of playing cards, determine the number of unique house of cards configurations that can be built, adhering to the rules that triangles are formed by two cards leaning against each other, a horizontal card must be placed between adjacent triangles in a row, triangles on higher rows must rest on horizontal cards from the previous row, and each triangle occupies the leftmost available spot in the row.
statement: Given an integer n representing the number of playing cards, determine the number of unique house of cards configurations that can be built, adhering to the rules that triangles are formed by two cards leaning against each other, a horizontal card must be placed between adjacent triangles in a row, triangles on higher rows must rest on horizontal cards from the previous row, and each triangle occupies the leftmost available spot in the row. Houses are considered distinct if they differ in the number of cards in any row.
constraints: A row with k adjacent triangles uses 3*k-1 cards.
Higher rows must contain fewer triangles, so each allowable row size 2,5,8,... may be used at most once.
Count distinct sets of row card counts totaling exactly n.
hints: Each possible row consumes a distinct card count congruent to two modulo three.
This is a subset-sum count using each row size at most once.
Initialize ways[0]=1; for row_cards=2,5,8,... update totals downward; return ways[n].
Downward updates prevent reusing a row size, and every selected subset corresponds uniquely to strictly decreasing triangle counts across house rows.
editorial: Downward updates prevent reusing a row size, and every selected subset corresponds uniquely to strictly decreasing triangle counts across house rows.

tests.explanation: The distinct row-card sets {2,14} and {5,11} both total sixteen, giving two houses.
One two-card triangle forms the only possible house.
